items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: Ah, Clay Robinson. I'll never forget him, God bless him. He was a very (big) something -- six foot seven.

ctx.x: quite known. He had taught most of the musicians in and around Washington, you know? And I'm trying to think. Let me see, brother, well there was James Miller. I worked with all the brothers, at one time or another, the Miller Brothers. They say This is the Miller brothers, and everybody will know who you're talking about. I'm trying to think who else was in there.

Ah, Clay Robinson. I'll never forget him, God bless him. He was a very (big) something -- six foot seven. He had his bass tuba. Well, back in those days -- I don't know if you remember. Guys used to take a blue light, a red light, and put it in the bell of a bass horn?
